description: Experimental design is a cross-domain workflow-planning primitive for planning studies before data collection. Use it for randomization, blocking, stratification, controls, factorial and fractional-factorial designs, response-surface optimization, crossover or cluster designs, plate layouts, replication, and pseudoreplication risk checks.
capabilities: Choose an experimental design from the question, treatment structure, unit of randomization, and nuisance factors.
Plan randomization, blocking, stratification, and run-order controls.
Separate true replication from repeated measurements to avoid pseudoreplication.
Hand off the selected design to statistical-power and statistical-analysis consumers.
requirements: A stated research question, response variable, treatment factors, and independent experimental unit.
Known nuisance factors such as batch, day, site, plate, operator, or instrument.
Downstream sample-size or analysis primitive for quantitative power or model fitting.
